build.test_boundary: Host state-machine and production Activity checks use Android platform fakes. They do not prove real OEM recovery.

agent.name: Muse
agent.source_of_results: Actual original-chat task receipts, with independent read-only maintenance state/log samples. Full cloud tool trace and raw screenshots were not exported.

preparation_and_prior_failures: Earlier candidates could not dismiss this phone's keyguard. Maintainer inspection found the OEM Show on lock screen setting disabled; the setting was enabled through normal system UI.

On code60 after that setting change, Muse visually verified two screen-off recoveries, a calculator result and return home. Following an ordinary reboot, the original pairing reconnected; the first observed reconnection was within 149 seconds, a polling observation rather than a bound.
That reboot stopped at a real SIM PIN prompt. Code60 misclassified it as dismissible keyguard. No PIN was tried by the maintainer or AI.
The same-signature code61 upgrade used authorized USB maintenance and retained the pairing. This installation is not evidence of a cloud-only upgrade.

code61_sim_authentication_check.scope: Actual SIM-only secure keyguard on this phone; not every combination of SIM and device authentication.

code61_after_owner_authentication.owner_action: Owner completed SIM PIN verification before the round. Fresh maintenance state was nonsecure keyguard and Dozing.

sms.boundary: A bounded GUI inspection of existing carrier notifications, not proof that every SMS source or future OTP is covered.

code61_after_owner_authentication.maintenance_observation: Read-only system state and filtered recovery logs; no UiAutomation dump or task substitution.
